newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 5.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
BIHAR GOVERNOR URGED NOT TO SANCTION PROSECUTION

Bihar chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav called on the governor and sought to make out a strong case against according sanction for his prosecution in the fodder scam. He cited a Supreme Court stay order in the Tamil Nadu face-off of 1995. Yadav took the stand that the issue of granting sanction to prosecute a chief minister still awaited a ruling by a full constitutional bench of the highest court.
The Times Of India
PRIME MINISTER ASSURES PUNJAB ON SHARING LOAN BURDEN

Prime Minister I.K. Gujral assured Punjab that the entire country would share the burden of 85 billion rupee loan incurred by the state in fighting militancy. The state government was demanding complete waiver of the loan since the entire expenditure was incurred to combat militancy in Punjab.
The Economic Times
ANOTHER GOOD MONSOON MAY BRING 193 MT FOODGAIN IN ITS TRAIL

The country was poised for its 10th successive good monsoon. The Agriculture Ministry was optimistic that grain production, which declined to 185 million tonnes in the previous year, would top 190 million tonnes this year. Sources said the Meteorological Department had already indicated a normal monsoon. The official monsoon forecast, however, would be made public by the department in the last week of May.
TATAS TO INCREASE THEIR STAKE IN TATA POWER TO 19.87 PCT

The Tatas would increase their stake in Tata Power Co (TPCL) to 19.87 percent from 15.76 percent. This comes in the wake of Tata Electric Companies' (TEC) declared intention to buy out TISCO's three billion rupee Jojobera power plant through a blend of preference equity and bonds issues. TEC proposed to finance the acquisition through a one billion rupee TPCL preference issue to TISCO and a two billion rupee bond issue.
NAPHTHA POWER PROJECTS TOLD TO KEEP IMPORT OPTION OPEN

The first set of fuel allocation letters, issued by the Petroleum Ministry, indicated all liquid fuel based power companies would have to make standby arrangements for fuel imports in case the oil companies failed to keep their supply commitments. The supply price of naphtha was fixed at the non-subsidised price under the administered price mechanism. Fuel imports by the power companies would be allowed under the prevalent import policy of the government.
Financial Express
POWER REGULATORY PANELS' DECISIONS TO BE BINDING ON STATES

In a bid to bail out the subsidy-ridden state electricity boards, the minister of state for power would like to make power tariff recommendations of the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERC) binding on state governments. The Power Ministry was in the process of preparing a cabinet note on the two-tier electricity regulatory commissions. The commissions at the states would fix tariffs for all categories of electricity consumers.
WHITE PAPER ON SUBSIDIES SOON: FINANCE MINISTER

The government would come out with a white paper on subsidies shortly to initiate a public debate on the subject, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram announced. Chidambaram said a 51 percent cut in the subsidy on non-merit goods would lead to the elimination of the country's entire fiscal deficit.
